Rashi on Bava Metzia 18a:10:1.hebrew: מצאו לאלתר - התם (גיטין כז:) מפרש: כדי שתעבור שיירא ותשרה, ובתוך כך ליכא למימר משיירא שעברה שם נפל, שהרי לא שהה שיעור שתחנה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 18a:10:1.english: He found it immediately - There (Gittin 27b) [the Gemara] explains: [within the time it takes] for a caravan to pass by and encamp, and within that [time] one cannot say [that] it fell from a caravan that passed through there, for he did not delay the amount [of time] for it to encamp.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 18a:12:1.hebrew: ואפילו במקום כו' - לאו רבה קא מסיק, אלא גמרא הוא דקאמר לן דכי אמר רבה במקום שהשיירות מצויות, לא אמר אלא כשהוחזקו בעיר אחת שנכתב בה הגט שנים ששמותיהן שוין ושמות נשותיהן שוות:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 18a:12:1.english: And even in a place, etc. - It is not Rabbah who is concluding [this statement]; rather, it is the Gemara that is telling us that when Rabbah said "in a place where caravans are common," he only said [so] where [it] has been established in the one city in which the bill of divorce was written [that there are] two [men] whose names are identical and whose wives' names are identical.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 18a:13:1.hebrew: דאי לא תימא הכי - דרבה תרתי בעי, קשיא דרבה אדרבה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 18a:13:1.english: For if you do not say so - that Rabbah requires both [conditions], [then] there is a contradiction between [one statement of] Rabbah and [another statement of] Rabbah.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 18a:13:2.hebrew: בי דינא דרב הונא - במקום שהוא יושב ודן, ומתוך שהכל רגילין אצלו לדון, הוי ליה מקום שהשיירות מצויות שם:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 18a:13:2.english: The court of Rav Huna - In the place where he sits and judges; and since everyone is accustomed [to come] to him for judgment, it is [considered] a place where caravans are commonly found.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 18a:1:1.hebrew: מאי גובה את הכל - מאחר שלא התנה עמה כלום, מהו התוספת:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 18a:1:1.english: What [is meant by] "she collects all" - Since he did not stipulate anything with her, what is the additional amount?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 18a:2:1.english: He does not enter acute mourning - Acute mourning does not take effect upon him with regard to the prohibition of eating sacrificial food.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 18a:2:2.hebrew: ולא מטמא לה - אם כהן הוא, דכתיב (ויקרא כא) "כי אם לשארו", והיינו אשתו; והאי לאו שארו הוא, דלא באו עדיין לידי קירוב בשר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 18a:2:2.english: Nor may he become ritually impure for her - [This applies] if he is a priest, as it is written (Leviticus 21): "except for his kin [she'ero]," and that [refers to] his wife; and this [betrothed woman] is not his kin [she'ero], since they have not yet come to closeness of flesh [i.e., marital intimacy].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 18a:2:3.hebrew: ולא מטמאה לו - לאו משום כהונה קאמר, דאין כהנות מוזהרות על הטומאה, דכתיב (שם) "בני אהרן". אלא, אינה זקוקה לטמא לו — לא כהנת ולא ישראלית — שמצוה להתעסק בשבעה מתי מצוה האמורים בפרשה, דכתיב: "לה יטמא", ותניא: "לה יטמא" — מצוה, ואם לא רצה, מטמאין אותו על כרחו, ומעשה ביוסף הכהן כו' בתורת כהנים:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 18a:2:3.english: And she does not become ritually impure for him - [The Tanna] is not saying [this] because of priesthood [laws], for priestesses are not warned against [contracting] ritual impurity, as it is written (there): "The sons of Aaron" [and not the daughters of Aaron]. Rather, [it means] she is not obligated to become ritually impure for him — neither a priestess nor an Israelite woman — as it is a commandment to occupy oneself with [burying] the seven deceased relatives [whom it is a] commandment [to bury] that are stated in the [Torah] portion, as it is written: "For her he shall become impure" [Leviticus 21:3]; and it is taught [in a Baraita]: "For her he shall become impure" — [this is] a commandment, and if he does not want [to do so], they defile him against his will, and [there is] the incident with Yosef the Kohen, etc., in Torat Kohanim.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 18a:2:4.hebrew: מתה אינו יורשה - דירושת הבעל נפקא לן מ"שארו הקרוב אליו ממשפחתו וירש אותה" וגו' בב"ב (דף קיא:), והא לאו שארו הוא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 18a:2:4.english: [If] she dies, he does not inherit her - For a husband's inheritance [of his wife] is derived from [the verse], "his relative who is closest to him of his family, and he shall inherit it," etc., in Bava Batra (111b), and this [betrothed woman] is not his relative.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 18a:4:1.hebrew: אלא אביי - דאמר לעיל לאו מילתא היא דאמרי, מגופא דמתני' דהוציאה גט — משום דהיא גופא קשיא ליה — הדר ביה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 18a:4:1.english: Rather, Abaye - who said earlier, "What I said is nothing" — because of the Mishnah itself of "[if] she produced a bill of divorce," since that itself was difficult for him, he retracted.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 18a:4:2.hebrew: דאי ס"ד - דטעמא לאו משום דאין טוענין אחר מעשה ב"ד הוא, אלא משום דגט היינו כתובה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 18a:4:2.english: Because if it enters your mind - that the reason is not because one does not plead against an act of the court, but rather because a bill of divorce is [her] marriage contract.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 18a:4:3.english: Is a maneh [or] two hundred [dinars] written in a bill of divorce - That we should say it proves the debt?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 18a:5:1.english: It is as though it is written in it - For it is a settled matter for us that a ketubah is one hundred [or] two hundred [zuz].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 18a:7:1.hebrew: אטו כל דמגבי בבי דינא מגבי לה - וכי כל הפורע חוב בא לב"ד? במקום שפרע לה, לא היו ב"ד שיכתבו לו כן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 18a:7:1.english: Does everyone who collects [payment] collect it in court - Does everyone who pays a debt come to court? In the place where he paid her, there was no court to write thus for him.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 18a:9:2.hebrew: נותנין - ואפילו נמצא לזמן מרובה משנפל, ולא חיישינן שמא גט אחר הוא ששמותיהן שוין ומאדם אחר נפל:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 18a:9:2.english: [They] give [it] - And even if it was found a long time after it fell, and we are not concerned that perhaps it is another document, [where] their names are identical and it fell from another person.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 18a:10:1.hebrew: לאלתר כשר - אפילו אביי, דחייש לתרי יצחק אפילו היכא דלא הוחזק (יבמות דף קטו:), בגט שמצאו לאלתר לא חייש, דהתם הוי כמו לזמן מרובה, דלא שייך התם לאלתר:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 18a:10:1.english: Immediately, [it is] valid - Even Abaye, who is concerned for [the possibility of] two [men named] Yitzchak even where [two such men] are not established [to exist] (Yevamot 115b), is not concerned in [the case of] a bill of divorce that one found immediately, for there it is like [finding it] after a long time, since [the concept of] "immediately" does not apply there.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 18a:12:1.hebrew: והוא שהוחזקו - תימה: אמאי לא מוקי אידי ואידי שהשיירות מצויות, ומתני' בלא הוחזקו, דהשתא הוי דומיא דסיפא ד"כל מעשה ב"ד" דמיירי בהכי? וי"ל דעובדא דבסמוך, דהוי בבי דינא דרב הונא, הוי ברישא, ואשמועינן דבלא הוחזקו יחזיר אפי' שיירות מצויות; והכא אשמועינן דאם הוחזקו נמי יחזיר, אם אין שיירות מצויות. וא"ת: ומאי טעמא יחזיר לאשה, כיון שיש שני יוסף בן שמעון בעיר? וי"ל: כיון שאנו יודעים שזה אבד גט כאן, אין לחוש שגם האחר איבד, כיון שאין שיירות מצויות. ושמעתין אתיא כר"א, דלרבי מאיר, כיון שהוחזקו שני יוסף בן שמעון, אין הגט כשר עד שיהא מוכיח מתוכו שהוא של זה, כדמוכח פרק כל הגט (גיטין דף כד:), דתנן: "כתב לגרש את הגדולה לא יגרש בו את הקטנה", ודייק: "הא גדולה מצי לגרש, מני? ר"א היא", ובעדי מסירה — משמע דלר"מ אפילו גדולה לא מצי מגרש. וההוא דהמגרש (שם דף פו:), דשני גיטין שוין שנתערבו, ומוקי כר"מ — מיירי במשולשים, דמוכיח מתוכו [וע"ע תוס' גיטין כד: ד"ה בעדי]:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 18a:12:1.english: And this is [only] where it has been established - This is puzzling: Why does [Rabba] not establish both [our Mishnah and the Mishnah in Gittin as referring to a place] where caravans are common, and [distinguish that] our Mishnah [is referring to a case] where [two people with the same name] have not been established, for then it would be similar to the latter clause of "any court enactment," which speaks of such [a case]? And one can answer that the incident below, which occurred in the court of Rav Huna, was [stated] first, and it teaches us that where [two people with the same name] have not been established, one returns [the document] even when caravans are common; and here [Rabba] teaches us that even if they have been established, one also returns it, if caravans are not common. And if you ask: What is the reason one may return [the bill of divorce] to the woman, since there are two [men named] Yosef ben Shimon in the city? One can answer: Since we know that this one lost a bill of divorce here, we need not be concerned that the other [man] also lost [one], since caravans are not common. And our passage accords with Rabbi Elazar, for according to Rabbi Meir, once two [men named] Yosef ben Shimon have been established [in the city], the bill of divorce is not valid unless it is evident from within [the document itself] that it belongs to this [particular] one, as is proven in the chapter [entitled] Kol HaGet (Gittin 24b), where we learned in the Mishnah: "[If] he wrote [a bill of divorce] to divorce the older [wife], he may not divorce the younger [wife] with it," and [the Gemara] infers: "Thus, he may divorce the older [wife with it]; whose [view] is this? It is [that of] Rabbi Elazar," and [it works] through the witnesses to the delivery — implying that according to Rabbi Meir, he cannot even divorce the older [wife with it]. And that [case] in [the chapter entitled] HaMegaresh (ibid., 86b), of two identical bills of divorce that became mixed up, which [the Gemara] establishes according to Rabbi Meir — that refers to [bills of divorce] with three generations [of names], where it is evident from within [the document itself] [see also Tosafot on Gittin 24b, s.v. "Be'edei"].

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 18a:4:1.hebrew: אטו גט מנה ומאתים כתיב ביה - תימה, היכי מוכח דאפילו במקום שכותבין כתובה דגביא אפי' כי לא נקיטא כתובה? דלמא הכא במקום שאין כותבין, וגביא בשטר גט, וכותבין בגט "שטרא דנן" כו', כדסבר (רבא) [רב] בפ' הכותב (כתובות דף פט:), ואביי נמי לוקמא הכי! אי נמי: נוקי במקום שאין כותבין כתובה, וגביא בעדי הגט, אבל גט לא קרעינן משום דבעיא לאנסובי ביה, והוי כמו היכא דלא אפשר דכותבין שובר; אבל במקום שכותבין כתובה — לא יפרע עד שתוציא שטר כתובה מידה, או משום שיהא נאמן לומר "פרעתי" דלא כרבי יוחנן, או משום דאין כותבין שובר! ועוד: כיון דמן אלמנה מן הנשואין במקום שאין כותבין לא בעי לאוכוחי, כמו שפי' לעיל (בבא מציעא דף יז: ד"ה אלמנה) — איך מוכח מגרושה מן הנישואין במקום שאין כותבין, כיון דגט לאו היינו כתובה, ומשום דבעינא לאנסובי ביה פשיטא דאין נאמן לומר "פרעתי", כיון דלא ניתקנה כתובה באותו מקום? וי"ל, דלאביי מתניתין קשיתיה, דתנן: "כתובה ואין עמה גט" — אלמא במקום שכותבין כתובה עסקינן, דאין סברא להעמיד שכן אירע שכתב לה בעבור אהבתה; לכך פריך: כיון שיש לה כתובה ואין מוציאה רק גט, לימא "פרעתי"! אלא ודאי לא אמר כלום, וכותבין שובר:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 18a:4:1.english: Is one hundred or two hundred [zuz] written in a bill of divorce? - This is astonishing: how does [the Gemara] prove that even in a place where they write a ketubah, she collects even when she does not hold a ketubah? Perhaps here [we are dealing] with a place where they do not write [a ketubah], and she collects with the document of the get, and they write in the get "This document..." etc., as Rav holds in the chapter [entitled] Hakotev (Ketubot 89b), and Abaye too should establish it thus! Alternatively, let us establish [the Mishnah] in a place where they do not write a ketubah, and she collects through the witnesses of the get, but we do not tear the get because she needs it to remarry with it, and it is like a case where it is not possible [to tear the document], where they write a receipt; but in a place where they write a ketubah — he should not pay until she produces the ketubah document from her hand, either because he would be believed to say "I paid," contrary to Rabbi Yochanan, or because they do not write a receipt! And furthermore, since from a widow from marriage in a place where they do not write [a ketubah] he did not want to prove [it], as we explained above (Bava Metzia 17b, s.v. Almanah) — how does he prove [it] from a divorcee from marriage in a place where they do not write [a ketubah], since a get is not a ketubah, and because she needs it to remarry with it, it is obvious that he is not believed to say "I paid," since a ketubah was not instituted in that place? And one can say that for Abaye, [the wording of] the Mishnah posed a difficulty to him, as we learned: "a ketubah without a get" — thus, we are dealing with a place where they write a ketubah, for it is not reasonable to establish [the Mishnah as referring to a case] where it happened that he wrote [a ketubah] for her out of his love for her; therefore he asks: since she has a ketubah and only produces a get, let him say "I paid"! Rather, he certainly has said nothing, and they write a receipt.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 18a:9:1.hebrew: הא אמר תנו נותנין - וא"ת: מנלן? דלמא אפילו אמר "תנו" אין נותנין! והא דקתני "נמלך", ה"ק: ונמלך שלא ליתנן, ומחמת כן לא חשש לשמור ונאבד, ועכשיו רוצה לחזור ולגרשה, דסבר שזהו הגט שאבד ממנו ואמר "תנו", ואפילו הכי אין נותנין, דשמא אין זה גיטו אלא נפל מאחר ששמו כשמו; אבל לא נמלך לכתחילה מלגרשה וגרשה, מחזירין לה הגט לראיה אפי' אינו שלה. וי"ל: דדייק מדלא קתני "כתובים היו ולא נתנן", ומדקתני "ונמלך" — משמע שחושש שמא אינו רוצה עתה לגרשה, אבל אם אמר "תנו לה" — נותנים, ואין לחוש שמא מאחר נפל. וא"ת: ומנלן "ואפי' לזמן מרובה"? דלמא לאלתר דוקא, כדפריך ר' זירא לקמן! ור' זירא גופיה מנלן דיחזיר לאשה אפילו לזמן מרובה, וממה פשוט לו דברייתא קאמר לזמן מרובה יותר ממתני'? וי"ל: דמברייתא משמע דבזמן שהבעל מודה יחזיר לאשה אפי' לזמן מרובה, דאי לאלתר דוקא — פשיטא! אבל במתני' מצי למימר לאלתר דוקא, ד"אם אמר תנו נותנין" אינו מפורש במתני', והיא גופה אתא לאשמועינן דלא יחזיר, דחיישינן לשמא נמלך. אבל רבה דייק מדקתני "ונמלך" ולא קתני "כתובין היו ולא נתן", א"כ אתא לאשמועינן "אם אמר תנו נותנין", והיינו אפי' לזמן מרובה, דאי לאלתר — פשיטא. וא"ת: והלא אפילו אי הוי לאלתר, הוי חידוש, דלא חיישינן דלמא כתב בניסן ולא נתן עד תשרי, כדפריך לקמן (בבא מציעא דף יט.)! וכן לקמן (עמוד ב), דפריך על רבי ירמיה דמוקי כגון דקאמרי עדים כו': "מאי למימרא?" — לימא דקא משמע לן דלא חיישינן דלמא כתב בניסן כו'! וי"ל: דס"ל כמאן דאמר אין לבעל פירות משעת חתימה, ואז ליכא חידוש דכתב בניסן ולא נתן עד תשרי, דאפילו הכי שפיר טרפה. ועוד י"ל, דרבי זירא דייק אפי' לזמן מרובה מדקתני "בזמן שהבעל מודה יחזיר לאשה", משמע שמודה שממנה נפל וכבר גירשה בו. ואי לאלתר דוקא, א"כ צ"ל שראינו הגט בידה, דאי לא ראינו — א"כ במה אנו יודעין שהוא לאלתר? ואחרי שראינו הגט בידה, הרי כבר מגורשת; פשיטא דיחזיר, ומאי קא משמע לן? והלא אפילו לא גיטה הוא זה — ניתן לה לראייה! ואין הבעל מודה נמי אמאי לא יחזיר? אלא ודאי מיירי שלא ראינו הגט בידה, וקמשמע לן דאע"פ דחיישינן שמא מבעל נפל ועדיין לא גירשה, תתגרש עתה בהחזרת הגט, ולא חיישינן שמא מאחר נפל; א"כ הוי אפי' לזמן מרובה, כיון דלא ידעינן ממי נפל — מן הבעל או מן האשה. ורבה דייק דמתני' נמי אפי' לזמן מרובה, דומיא דשטרי חליצה ומיאונין דיחזיר אפי' לזמן מרובה; דלאלתר היינו שראינו בידה — פשיטא, כיון דחלצה נחזיר לה לראיה אפילו אינו שלה! אלא מיירי שלא ראינו בידה ואף לא ידעינן שחלצה, והיינו לזמן מרובה, ודומיא דהכי משמע ליה דמיירי ברישא. ורבי זירא לא מוקי לה דומיא דסיפא:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 18a:9:1.english: "But [if] he said 'Give,' we give [it]" - And if you ask: From where do we [derive this]? Perhaps even if he said "Give," we do not give [it]! And that which [the Mishnah] teaches "reconsidered," this is what it is saying: "and he reconsidered not to give them," and because of that he was not careful to guard [it] and it was lost, and now he wants to go back and divorce her, for he thinks that this is the bill of divorce that was lost from him and [therefore] says "Give," yet even so we do not give [it], for perhaps this is not his bill of divorce, but rather it fell from another [man] whose name is like his name; whereas [if] he did not initially reconsider divorcing her and he [already] divorced her, we return the bill of divorce to her as proof even [if] it is not hers! And one can answer: [The Gemara] infers [this] from the fact that it does not teach "they were written and he did not give them," and from the fact that it teaches "and he reconsidered" — this implies that it is concerned lest he does not want to divorce her now, whereas if he said "Give [it] to her," we give [it], and we need not be concerned lest it fell from another [man]. And if you ask: From where do we [derive] "and even [after] a long time"? Perhaps [it refers] specifically to immediately, as R. Zeira challenges below! And R. Zeira himself — from where does he [derive] that one returns [it] to the woman even [after] a long time, and why is it more obvious to him that the Baraita is speaking of a long time than the Mishnah? And one can answer: From the Baraita it is implied that when the husband admits [it], one returns [it] to the woman even [after] a long time, for if [it referred] specifically to immediately, [that would be] obvious! But in the Mishnah one could say [it refers] specifically to immediately, for "if he said 'Give,' we give [it]" is not stated explicitly in the Mishnah, and [the Mishnah] itself comes to teach us that he should not return [it], because we are concerned lest he reconsidered. Rabbah, however, infers [it] from the fact that it teaches "and he reconsidered" and does not teach "they were written and he did not give [them]"; if so, it comes to teach us [that] if he said "Give," we give [it], and that is even [after] a long time, for if immediately — [it would be] obvious. And if you ask: Even if it were immediately, wouldn't there [still] be a novelty, namely that we are not concerned lest he wrote [it] in Nisan and did not give [it] until Tishrei, as [the Gemara] challenges below (Bava Metzia 19a)! And similarly below (18b), where [the Gemara] challenges R. Yirmiyah, who establishes [the Mishnah] in a case where witnesses say, etc.: "Why state it?" — let it say that it teaches us that we are not concerned lest he wrote [it] in Nisan, etc.! And one can answer: He holds like the one who says the husband does not have [rights to] the produce from the time of signing, and then there is no novelty [regarding] "he wrote [it] in Nisan and did not give [it] until Tishrei," for even so she may properly seize [encumbered property with it]. And furthermore one can answer that R. Zeira infers "even [after] a long time" from the fact that it teaches "when the husband admits, he returns [it] to the woman," which implies that he admits that it fell from her and he already divorced her with it. And if [it referred] specifically to immediately, if so, we would have to say that we saw the bill of divorce in her hand, for if we did not see [it] — if so, how do we know that it is immediate? And once we saw the bill of divorce in her hand, she is already divorced; [it is] obvious that he returns [it], so what is it teaching us? Even if this were not her bill of divorce, we would give [it] to her as proof! And even if the husband did not admit [it], why wouldn't he return [it]? Rather, it certainly deals [with a case] where we did not see the bill of divorce in her hand, and it teaches us that even though we are concerned that perhaps it fell from the husband and he has not yet divorced her, she will be divorced now through the return of the bill of divorce, and we are not concerned lest it fell from another [man]; if so, it is even [after] a long time, since we do not know from whom it fell — from the husband or from the woman. And Rabbah infers that the Mishnah also [refers] even [after] a long time, similar to documents of chalitzah and refusals [of marriage], where one returns [them] even [after] a long time; for "immediately" means that we saw [it] in her hand — [which is] obvious, since she performed chalitzah we would return [it] to her as proof even [if] it is not hers! Rather, it deals [with a case] where we did not see [it] in her hand and we also do not know that she performed chalitzah, and that is [after] a long time, and it seems to him that the first clause likewise deals [with such a case].
